review.note: Independent third review (review-03.md) accepted after two NOT_ACCEPT rounds (review-01: corrupt non-interleaved JPEG grids and same-bytes concurrent import; review-02: interlaced PNG filter bytes unchecked). Review-03 re-proved every blocker fix: 42/42 Adam7 per-row corruptions refused with Pillow/libpng agreeing on 90 files, SOF0/SOF1-only frame markers, duplicate component ids, MCU cap 10, and source.committed/source.retired versions matching landed commits. Non-blocking items are listed in review-03.md: zlib FCHECK/FDICT unchecked, ff c8 marker accepted, MCU cap sums frame rather than scan components (stricter), 6-way concurrent imports can exhaust the retry budget (fail-closed), and receipt wording on libjpeg duplicate-id agreement.

interface.persistence: Through the V6-06 LocalRepository commit (CAS on matter version, actor/tenant ownership, activity allowlist). Drawing bytes are V6-10 asset + blob rows (sha256, byteLength). Drawing rows and append-only FigureSetRevision rows (validated by figureSetRevisionSchema on read) live in the blobs store under the drawings/ and figures/ namespaces (V6-11 precedent). Activity actions: source.committed {version}, source.retired {version}, figures.bound {version, count}; version is the matter version the commit writes. Drawing rows and figure-set revision rows are written outside the matter commit (it cannot carry namespaced rows) under an id unique to each attempt, so a writer that loses the commit race removes only its own row.

The orchestrator's working copy (git blob c997eeae5517e9bd6731b76776f605f666e6520e) already imports and mounts Figures in both pages; the typecheck and build below ran against it.

decisions.subject: Seeding targets directly in tests
decisions.decision: Accepted. No ticket before V6-12 creates targets; the harness writes the targets in the seeded matter commit and the UI receives targetId null until a target-creation ticket lands.

decisions.subject: Activity actions for drawings
decisions.decision: Accepted. Import reuses source.committed ({version}), delete reuses source.retired ({version}), binds use figures.bound {version, count}. These are listed contract actions; no new action names are added. version is the matter version written by the same commit, so the event names the state change it belongs to (review-02 non-blocking 4).

decisions.subject: Clearing confirmations/checks/approvals after BindFigures
decisions.decision: Not missing: V6-05 derives it. confirmation.ts (isConfirmationCurrent, currentConfirmations via sameSnapshot), gate.ts (sameSnapshot incl. figureRevisionId) and revision.ts (isCurrent, isInputStale, currentInput) all treat a changed target.figureRevisionId as stale. figure-currency.test.mjs proves it through the real domain functions; S02-A08 is now covered.

decisions.subject: V6-04 revision module vs figure-set storage
decisions.decision: Accepted. revision.ts models draft revisions that consume figure sets; append-only FigureSetRevision rows validated by figureSetRevisionSchema are owned by drawings.ts. figure-currency.test.mjs proves the minted ids interoperate with revision.ts (saveRevision binds them, adoptInputs moves to the new id, restoreRevision restore_bound finds the persisted old set by id and copies its entries and hash).

decisions.subject: Rows under drawings/ and figures/ in the blobs store
decisions.decision: Accepted for R1, following the V6-11 parse-row precedent. Dedicated tables are an R2 follow-up (see limitations).

decisions.subject: Interlaced PNG filter bytes (review-02 B1)
decisions.decision: Fixed. verifyPngData builds one row list from the Adam7 pass geometry and walks it with the same MAX_PNG_FILTER check as non-interlaced rows. Every pass row's first byte must be 0-4; anything else is BAD_DRAWING before import can store, bind or pass the export gate. The walk asserts its final offset equals the inflated length, and the old interlaced early return is gone. Independent decode outside the repo: Pillow 12.1.0 (libpng) decodes drawing-interlaced-valid.png as 33x7 RGB and raises on drawing-interlaced-bad-filter.png.

decisions.subject: JPEG coding process and frame shape (review-02 non-blocking 1-3)
decisions.decision: Fixed. Only SOF0 (baseline) and SOF1 (extended sequential Huffman) frames are accepted; every other frame marker is BAD_DRAWING (SOF2 keeps its progressive message, the rest share a generic unsupported-coding message). parseFrame rejects a repeated component id, and an interleaved scan whose frame components sum(h*v) exceeds 10 is refused per T.81 B.2.3.

Eight V6-12-A02 tests and two V6-12 B1 tests pass through the pure checkFigureExportGate and the import/bind validators: corrupt/lying images refused with no writes (now including a 4000x3000 non-interleaved 4:2:0 file whose luma scan holds 47,000 of 187,500 blocks, and a 3-component frame with only component 1 scanned, both BAD_DRAWING; a valid non-interleaved 4:2:0 file with DRI is accepted at 40x16); deleted drawing, digest mismatch and missing blob give MISSING_BYTES; a draft on an older set gives STALE_BINDING and an unaddressed reference RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, with filesAvailable still true because every byte is present; the gate writes nothing (store dump equal); non-1..n numbering refused by BindFigures with no writes; a persisted legacy revision with repeated numbers is reported as DUPLICATE_FIGURE_NUMBER with filesAvailable true and is not repaired; a stale base gives INPUT_STALE with currentFigureRevisionId; a fromAssetId that is not an available asset of this matter is RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND with no writes. Review-02 additions: a valid Adam7 33x7 PNG is accepted, imports, binds and leaves the gate allowed, while the same image with one pass row's filter byte set to 7 is BAD_DRAWING and writes nothing; SOF3/SOF5/SOF6/SOF7/SOF9/SOF10/SOF11/SOF13/SOF14/SOF15 frame markers, a frame listing component id 1 twice, and an interleaved 4x4+1x1+1x1 (18-block) MCU are all BAD_DRAWING and write nothing.

Seven V6-12-A03 tests pass: duplicate import is refused or reused with no new asset/row/event; retrying a completed bind returns the persisted revision and appends nothing; a failed import leaves no partial state and the retry lands once; two concurrent imports of different bytes each land once through the version check; two concurrent imports of the same bytes give one asset, one drawing row and one source.committed event, one answer created and the other the duplicate refusal naming that row (every returned id resolves); two concurrent identical binds forced to both read the base before either writes leave the seed revision plus exactly one bind revision, the pointer on an existing row, one figures.bound event and a passing gate; a fresh repository over the same backend shows exactly the persisted library, binding and stale flag.

limitations: Browser run covers the library surface with targetId null only. Target-bound states (figure set, gate, set-missing, INPUT_STALE), the stale notice and the load-failure notice are not reachable in R1 through the UI (see browser.notReachable); they are covered by the server-rendered markup and domain tests only.
No target-creation command exists (D1); the harness seeds targets directly and the UI gets targetId null.

JPEG support is baseline/extended sequential Huffman (SOF0/SOF1) with DRI/RSTn, interleaved or one scan per component. Every other frame marker (SOF2 progressive, SOF3 lossless, SOF5/6/7 differential, SOF9/10/11 arithmetic, SOF13/14/15 differential arithmetic) is refused as BAD_DRAWING, as are a frame that lists one component id twice, an interleaved MCU with more than 10 data units (T.81 B.2.3), a component coded by more than one scan, and a frame component that no scan codes. Users must save such files as baseline JPEG or PNG.
R2 follow-up: dedicated storage tables for drawings and figure-set revisions. In R1 the rows live in the blobs store under the drawings/ and figures/ namespaces (D5).
No draft store exists yet, so the S02-A08 tests hold draft revisions, confirmations, check runs and approvals in V6-04/V6-05 domain state; only drawings and figure sets are persisted.
There are no thumbnails; the library shows name, decoder-verified dimensions, type, size and digest prefix only.

Deleted drawing bytes stay in the blobs store (review-01 finding 2; browser step 06 shows orphanBytesKept). readBlob refuses them because the asset is gone, but a purge path per contract §11 is still needed before R2.
verifyPngData inflates the whole IDAT in memory: a 16 MP 16-bit RGBA PNG needs about 128 MB (review-01 finding 9). It is inside the limits but heavy on mobile; a streaming row check is a follow-up.

Drawing rows and figure-set revision rows are written in their own transaction just before the matter commit, not inside it (LocalRepository.commit cannot carry namespaced rows). A crash between the two leaves an unreferenced row with an attempt-unique id; readers ignore it and it is never reused, but it is not swept.

Not changed (review-01 findings 6, 7, 10; review-02 finding 6): the gate surfaces only DUPLICATE_FIGURE_NUMBER from the numbering check (bindFigures refuses gaps and over-limit sets at write time); referencedFigureIds come from the caller until the export ticket derives them from DraftAST; zlib Adler-32, the zlib FCHECK/FDICT header fields and JPEG coefficient ranges are not checked.

blockers.fix: decodeBaselineScan measures a single-component scan on that component's own block grid, ceil(ceil(X*h/Hmax)/8) x ceil(ceil(Y*v/Vmax)/8), one block per MCU (DRI counts these); interleaved scans keep the frame MCU grid with h*v blocks per component. verifyJpegScan refuses a file in which any SOF component was not scanned before EOI. A component scanned by more than one scan fails closed as BAD_DRAWING.
tests: V6-12 B1 a non-interleaved scan is counted on its component's own block grid
V6-12 B1 every component the frame declares must be scanned before EOI

blockers.fix: storeDrawing mints a drawing id with a per-attempt nonce, deletes only its own row after a failed commit, and on VERSION_CONFLICT reloads and runs the sha256 duplicate check again, so the second caller gets the duplicate refusal (or the existing drawing with reuseExisting). bindFigures mints a per-attempt revision id, deletes only its own row after a failed pointer commit, and on VERSION_CONFLICT or INPUT_STALE re-reads: the same bind already landed (answer it), the target moved (INPUT_STALE), or only the version moved (write again; at most FIGURE_COMMIT_ATTEMPTS). Because revision ids are no longer derived from content, history is ordered by parent-chain depth, then createdAt, then id.

blockers.fix: verifyPngData no longer returns early for interlaced data. It builds the row list from the Adam7 pass geometry (seven passes, empty passes skipped, each row = 1 filter byte + ceil(passWidth*channels*depth/8) bytes) and walks every pass row through the same MAX_PNG_FILTER check the non-interlaced path uses. The walk asserts its final offset equals rows.byteLength; a filter byte above 4 is BAD_DRAWING before any write, so a corrupted interlaced PNG cannot be imported, bound or pass the export gate.
